components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Primary search trigger in the rail.

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Stops an active search while preserving partial leads.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { background: #c83e2b; color: #ffffff; padding: 8px 14px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 6px; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.84rem; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #c83e2b; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Bus Stop Plaque

components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: Mode filter chip for the accessible qualifying stops list.

narrative.overview: House Hunter adopts the visual discipline of Singapore HDB void-deck and town-centre wayfinding boards: high-contrast daylight porcelain panels, concrete framing, unmistakable stop-ID plaques, and honest spatial caveats. It refuses dark telemetry dashboards, property-portal listing chrome, and decorative glassmorphism so commuters can scan live searches on desktop and inspect saved 500 m housing-search zones outdoors at offline property viewings.
keyCharacteristics: Daylight-first porcelain and warm concrete shell paired with botanical green catchment zones
Rounded-square stop-ID plaques uniting interactive map markers, list rows, and journey detail cards
Strict tabular numerals for stop codes, tried/matched counters, dates, and boarding/arrival clocks
Unsoftened status tags and non-collapsible proximity caveats

rules.name: The Uniform Catchment Rule
rules.body: All 500 m circles render at full opacity inside one shared SVG layer whose parent pane sits at 0.34 opacity, so overlapping zones merge cleanly without double-darkening seams.

rules.name: The Unsoftened Caveat Rule
rules.body: Offline banners, Keep the app open notices, and Partial result tags use high-contrast amber paper (#fef3c7) with #78350f ink and #d97706 borders so critical limits never blend into decorative chrome.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: All counters (Stops tried, Matching stops), dates, clock times, ride durations, and stop IDs enforce font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so live updates never jitter.

rules.name: The Single-Boundary Elevation Rule
rules.body: Never stack a 1px card border underneath a soft drop shadow; choose a crisp border for docked surfaces or a shadow for floating map overlays.

dos: Do keep the keep-open notice visible before preview. Omit inventory dates from the interface and show the original search date only alongside verified journey evidence.
Do preserve uniform 500 m catchment opacity using one shared SVG renderer inside commuteZonePane.
Do keep Stops tried and Matching stops visually distinct in tabular figures.
donts: Don't add drop shadows to 1 px bordered rail panels or borders to shadowed floating overlays.
Don't use eyebrow labels, numbered section headers (01 / 02), one-sided accent bars on rounded boxes, or backdrop-filter glass blurs.
Don't gate saved offline map viewing behind OneMap sign-in.
